## What's Changed
* Integrate Windows scanning, drive picker and navigation fixes by @tobi in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/42
* build: pin the toolchain so a fresh clone can't fail on a stale default by @adi0x90 in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/30
* Steam libraries on a second drive show as media, not cache by @btsouth in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/33
* Switching between Size and Files keeps you in the same folder by @btsouth in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/34
* fix(windows): embed icon in executable by @rteoo in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/37
* fix: wire the mouse side buttons to back and forward by @fgrehm in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/39
* feat: read a whole NTFS drive from its file table when elevated by @mgpai22 in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/40
* feat: volume picker dialog and centered alert dialog popups by @ai94iq in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/41
* Cancel a scan in progress by @btsouth in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/35
* README: document the AUR packages by @DouglasdeMoura in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/27
* Fix macOS cmux launches without regressing Unicode arguments by @tobi in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/43
* macOS: keep command-line launches alive in cmux by @ashwch in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/23
* Fix repeated mount accounting and external SSD deletion guards by @tobi in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/44
* Count bind mounts and repeated mounts once by @btsouth in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/36
* feat: add saved Power Efficiency scan worker presets (3% faster, 53% less CPU at 8 threads) by @huntharo in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/63
* Flag a marked path whose name is not valid Unicode by @kevin9327 in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/52
* docs(readme): the t key cycles three modes, not two by @kuishou68 in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/46
* Show a size that rounds up to 1024 in the next unit by @kevin9327 in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/70
* test: wait for widening scans to finish before assertions by @huntharo in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/69
* Reveal a tile in the file manager on right-click by @aronchick in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/49
* Improves scan speed on macOS, better memory profile everywhere by @joshgosse in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/53
* fix(space): exclude foreign-volume marks from free-space projection by @itsmunzir in https://github.com/tobi/disktree/pull/56

detail.readme_excerpt:
# disktree

![disktree: a home directory as a treemap, coloured by kind of data, with reclaimable space hatched and the selection, findings and free space in the side panel](assets/screenshot.png)

Find what is filling a disk, mark what should go, and remove it — with the
volume's free space in view the whole time.

disktree is a treemap for Omarchy. Choose a local or SSH source, then a
mounted volume or directory; no scan starts until you explicitly accept.
It draws every directory as a nested mosaic sized by its real disk cost,
and lets you walk into it with the keyboard or the mouse. Mark as much as you
like; nothing happens until you review the list and commit, and the permanent
path always asks first.

Built with [GPUI](https://gpui-kit.com/) through
[gpui-omarchy](https://github.com/huacnlee/gpui-omarchy), so it follows your
Omarchy theme and behaves like the rest of the desktop.

## Install

Download `disktree-*-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` (`aarch64-linux` on ARM) from the
[latest release](https://github.com/tobi/disktree/releases/latest), unpack
it, and run `./install.sh` inside (or just copy `disktree` onto your
`PATH`). Or build it:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/tobi/disktree
cd disktree
make install
```

`make install` builds a release binary and puts three things under `~/.local`
(no root needed):

- `~/.local/bin/disktree`
- a desktop entry, so disktree is in the launcher and in a file manager's
  **Open with** for a directory (it adds a handler; it never becomes the
  default)
- an icon

`sudo make install PREFIX=/usr/local` installs system-wide; `make uninstall`
removes exactly what was installed.

On Arch, including Omarchy, disktree is in the AUR:
[`disktree`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/disktree) builds each release
from source, and
[`disktree-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/disktree-bin) installs
the release binary:

```sh
yay -S disktree-bin
```

If another installed version wins on `PATH`, the installer warns which one.
Run `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` and add that setting to your shell
configuration so the locally installed build takes precedence.

For Linux builds with embedded SSH helpers, also install the two Rust
standard-library targets (no external C cross-compiler is needed):

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
```

You need Rust 1.97 or newer and a Wayland or X11 session with a GPU that GPUI
can drive (Vulkan). Distributions often package an older Rust;
[rustup](https://rustup.rs) installs a current one. The repo pins 1.97 in
`rust-toolchain.toml`, so with rustup the right toolchain is fetched on the
first build even if `rustup default` points at something older.

### macOS

Download `disktree-*-aarch64-macos.zip` (`x86_64-macos` for an Intel Mac)
from the [latest release](https://github.com/tobi/disktree/releases/latest),
unzip it, and drag `disktree.app` into Applications. macOS 11 or newer.
